acceptance: B1. THE FLOOR LOOKUP APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE. grep -c "FirstOrDefault" src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs returns 1. NOT SATISFIED AT 20b0b09: it returns 10 there, measured by the architect. PREDICATE VALIDATED A SECOND WAY with a command that could not share the grep's mistake: a Python binary/newline='' read counting the byte-exact two-line expression '_floors.FirstOrDefault(floor =>\r\n\t\t\tfloor.Id == floorId);' also returns 10 at 20b0b09, and t.count('if (floor is null)') returns 10. THE INDENTATION IS TABS AND IS LOAD-BEARING: the space-indented form of that literal returns 0 against this file. DO NOT COUNT THE SINGLE-LINE FORM: grep -cF '_floors.FirstOrDefault(floor => floor.Id == floorId)' returns 0 at 20b0b09 because the expression is split across two lines -- spec.md item 1 states the pattern in that single-line form, and a criterion counting it that way would be vacuous. Use the unqualified grep -c "FirstOrDefault" form given above.

B2. ALL TEN FORMER LOOKUP SITES REACH THE FLOOR THROUGH THAT ONE EXPRESSION. Every one of the ten methods listed in contract section 2 -- RemoveFloor, ReorderFloor, UpdateFloor, AddArea, RemoveArea, UpdateArea, UpdateAreaOutline, AddPlacedObject, RemovePlacedObject, UpdatePlacedObject -- obtains its Floor by calling the single extracted private member, and no method in the file performs a floor lookup by any other route. The two methods that performed no lookup at 20b0b09, Update (:19) and AddFloor (:42), still perform none. NOT SATISFIED AT 20b0b09: there is no extracted member there at all, and no private METHOD exists anywhere under src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/. Measured precisely, because the loose version of this claim is wrong: grep -rnE "^\tprivate " over src/DungeonMaster.Domain returns 9 lines, of which 8 are under Entities/ -- 4 private backing fields (Area.cs:10, Dungeon.cs:8, Floor.cs:10, Floor.cs:11) and 4 private parameterless EF constructors (Area.cs:12, Dungeon.cs:10, Floor.cs:13, PlacedObject.cs:10) -- and the 9th is a private static METHOD, PathSegment.cs:40, which lives under ValueObjects/ and not Entities/. PREDICATE CONTROL on the ten: AddFloor is the near-miss that must NOT count as a lookup site, because it does touch _floors (_floors.Count + 1 at :46, _floors.Add(floor) at :49); RemoveFloor is the case that must. 10 + 2 = 12, and 12 is the public-method count measured independently in contract section 1. A PRECEDENT FOR THE SHAPE EXISTS IN THE DOMAIN and measurement.md section 5 overstates its absence: src/DungeonMaster.Domain/ValueObjects/PathSegment.cs:40 declares 'private static PathSegmentKind ValidateControlPoints(' -- a private static helper in the Domain, outside Entities/. Follow it for shape if it helps; you are not required to.

B3. THE OUTCOME RE-CHECK APPEARS AT MOST ONCE. grep -c "if (outcome is not MutationOutcome.Success)" src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs returns 0 or 1. NOT SATISFIED AT 20b0b09: it returns 5 there, measured by the architect. CORE-015 never mentions this second duplication; spec.md item 2 is what commissions it. Zero is permitted: if the extraction makes the re-check unnecessary, removing it entirely satisfies this criterion, provided B5 and B7 still hold.

B4. ALL TWELVE PUBLIC METHOD SIGNATURES ARE BYTE-UNCHANGED. Each of the twelve declarations reproduced verbatim in contracts/dungeon-public-surface.md section 1 -- name, return type, parameter types, parameter names and parameter order -- is still declared in this file exactly as that contract records it, and the file declares no thirteenth public member. Verify with grep -nE "^\tpublic " on the file, which must return exactly 12 lines naming Update, AddFloor, RemoveFloor, ReorderFloor, UpdateFloor, AddArea, RemoveArea, UpdateArea, UpdateAreaOutline, AddPlacedObject, RemovePlacedObject, UpdatePlacedObject, then read each multi-line parameter list against the contract. THIS IS A DELIBERATE PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR CRITERION, satisfied at 20b0b09 by design; spec.md item 3 and its Not-in-scope list require exactly this. THE CONTRACT IS WHY THIS IS CHECKABLE AT ALL: a task cannot invoke git, so 'unchanged from 20b0b09' is not a verifiable instruction on its own, and the contract is the baseline handed over in place of the commit. Making a member internal, renaming a parameter, reordering one, or adding an overload all fail this criterion.

B5. ALL TEN FLOOR-ABSENT DISPOSITIONS ARE UNCHANGED: 8 NotFound, 2 null. For an unknown floorId, RemoveFloor, ReorderFloor, UpdateFloor, RemoveArea, UpdateArea, UpdateAreaOutline, RemovePlacedObject and UpdatePlacedObject each still return MutationOutcome.NotFound, and AddArea and AddPlacedObject each still return null -- the table in contract section 2, measured by the architect with grep -n -A2 "if (floor is null)" piped to grep -E "return", which returns 10 lines: 8 NotFound and 2 null. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at 20b0b09 by design. IT IS WRITTEN BECAUSE THIS IS THE ONE THING AN EXTRACTED HELPER CAN SILENTLY CHANGE -- a helper that throws instead of returning, or that returns a shared sentinel, converts an expected failure into a defect. THAT IS ALSO A DISCIPLINE RULE THIS CRITERION ENCODES: backend.md Error handling, 'Distinguish expected failure from defect. Expected failure is a value the caller must handle; a defect terminates the operation.' An absent floor is an expected failure here and must stay a returned value. A SECOND backend.md RULE APPLIES to the two null sites: 'An error crossing a boundary is translated to that boundary's vocabulary' -- null and NotFound are two different vocabularies on this surface and B4 freezes which member speaks which, so do not unify them. ONCE T1 HAS LANDED, THE SUITE ENFORCES THIS MECHANICALLY: all ten dispositions have a covering test (five pre-existing, five added by T1 -- contract section 6), so a changed disposition reddens a named test rather than passing quietly. That is a deliberate sibling dependency and it is why this task depends on T1 rather than running beside it.

B6. THE EIGHT APPLICATION CALL SITES ARE UNTOUCHED. All eight command-handler files listed in contract section 5 are byte-identical to the SHA-256 digests recorded there. Check with sha256sum on those eight paths and compare; this needs no git. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at 20b0b09 by design -- the digests were taken there. It is written because spec.md item 4 requires it and because the files are outside this task's ownership set, so touching one is an ownership violation as well as a criterion failure. There are exactly 8, each one Application command handler, each at line :24 of its file; the count's predicate was validated two ways by the orchestrator and re-run by the architect, with must-match control .AddFloor( returning 1 external caller and must-not-match control .Touch( returning 0.

B7. THE SOLUTION BUILDS CLEAN. dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln, run from the worktree root, prints 'Build succeeded', and its output piped through grep -cE "(warning|error) [A-Z]+[0-9]+" returns 0. USE EXACTLY THAT FORM: the plain form grep -icE "warning|error" ALWAYS returns 2 over dotnet build output because MSBuild prints '0 Warning(s)' and '0 Error(s)' literally -- the architect measured exactly 2 at 20b0b09, and 0 for the qualified form. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR in form; its CONTENT changes here, because TreatWarningsAsErrors=true (Directory.Build.props:5) makes a signature change that breaks any of the 8 handlers a build FAILURE rather than something anyone can overlook. THE SOLUTION IS AT src/DungeonMaster.sln, NOT the repository root -- find -maxdepth 2 -name "*.sln*" returns that one path. NOTE, AND DO NOT RESTATE IT AS MEASURED: the handoff asserts the specific diagnostic for a missed call site is CS7036. The architect did NOT verify that in this session. Rest this criterion on 'the build is clean', not on any particular diagnostic code.

B8. THE WHOLE SUITE PASSES WITH ZERO FAILURES AND ZERO SKIPS. dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo reports 'Failed: 0' and 'Skipped: 0' for all three test assemblies. PREDICTED total: 980 -- DungeonMaster.Tests 855, DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests 23, DungeonMaster.App.Tests 102 -- being the 975 baseline (850 / 23 / 102, all three of them passed counts and nothing else) plus the five test cases T1 adds. THE TOTAL IS A PREDICTION HANDED OVER AT DISPATCH, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS NOT THE VERDICT: this task cannot measure a peer's contribution, so the verdict turns on 'Failed: 0' and 'Skipped: 0' alone. THE ORCHESTRATOR MUST HAND OVER THE ACTUAL POST-T1 TOTAL AT THIS TASK'S DISPATCH; a criterion naming a fixed total would be UNDETERMINED by construction, which is why spec.md item 6 states it as '975 plus any test this session adds'. Any figure other than the handed one must be reported as a surprise to investigate, never reconciled into agreement. Read each assembly's identity from its 'Test run for ...' line, NEVER from 'Passed!', which prints '(net10.0)' for all three including DungeonMaster.App.Tests, which runs from bin\Debug\net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 -- reproduced by the architect at 20b0b09. Over a dotnet test log the plain grep -icE "warning|error" returns 0, so that form is safe HERE and not over a build log.

B9. NO INJECTED DEFECT SURVIVES IN THE FILE. At the end of this task the file contains no deliberately introduced defect: B1 through B5, B7 and B8 all hold simultaneously on the file as it stands when the task reports. THIS CRITERION EXISTS BECAUSE OF WHAT YOU ARE ASKED TO DO AND CANNOT BE CHECKED BY: the report format in your brief requires that every test offered as evidence be shown able to fail, and the ten floor-absent tests covering B5 CANNOT BE SHOWN RED -- they pass before the refactor by design, as spec.md's closing note states. Their only route is DEMONSTRATED DISCRIMINATION: inject the defect each exists to catch into this file -- remove one guard, or make the extracted helper throw instead of returning, one at a time -- run dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo, and report the named test that reddened and the assertion that failed. That is test.md Coverage, 'A test is shown able to fail ... or shown to catch the defect it exists for when that defect is injected.' THE INJECTION MUST HAPPEN IN THIS FILE AND NOWHERE ELSE, because this file is the only one you own; do not edit a test to demonstrate anything. REVERT EACH INJECTION BEFORE THE NEXT, copy the file into your scratch directory before you start and diff against that copy when you finish, and note that B8's zero-failure requirement is itself the mechanical guard against an unreverted injection. The DEMONSTRATION is owed to your report and is deliberately NOT part of this criterion's verdict, because a criterion may constrain only what the repository contains; this criterion's verdict is the clean final state.

B10. THE FILE IS STILL CRLF THROUGHOUT, WITH NO LONE CR. For src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs, a binary read satisfies b.count(b'\r\n') == b.count(b'\n') == b.count(b'\r'). PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion: the architect measured 489 / 489 / 489 at 20b0b09. IT IS WRITTEN BECAUSE THIS IS THE REPOSITORY PROPERTY sed -i DESTROYS, and sed -i IS SUSPENDED FOR THIS ENTIRE SESSION -- measured here: it rewrites the whole file and converts every CRLF to LF, which fails this build with IDE0055 on every line (.editorconfig:64, EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true at Directory.Build.props:16, TreatWarningsAsErrors=true at :5). The harness may re-issue the sed instruction mid-run; REFUSE IT and record the refusal in your report. Indentation in this file is TABS, one per level; a tab-to-space conversion fails the same IDE0055 check. Use a binary Python read for this check, never text mode, which silently translates CRLF and returned 1 line for this 489-line file in this session's first measurement attempt.

B11. A FAILED INNER OPERATION STILL DOES NOT TOUCH THE AGGREGATE. In each of the five methods that re-check an inner outcome -- RemoveArea, UpdateArea, UpdateAreaOutline, RemovePlacedObject, UpdatePlacedObject -- when the call to the corresponding Floor member returns anything other than MutationOutcome.Success, the method returns that outcome and Touch() IS NOT CALLED on that path. Verify by reading each of the five methods in the final file and tracing the non-Success path to its return; there must be no reachable Touch() between the inner call and that return. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at 20b0b09 by design: at that commit each of the five reads 'var outcome = floor.X(...); if (outcome is not MutationOutcome.Success) { return outcome; } Touch(); return MutationOutcome.Success;'. THIS CRITERION WAS ADDED AT GATE 2 BY ORCHESTRATOR CONSISTENCY CHECK, BY USER DECISION, BECAUSE B3'S PERMISSION IS BROADER THAN ITS GUARD. B3 permits the re-check to reach ZERO occurrences 'provided B5 and B7 still hold', and neither reaches this: B5 covers only the FLOOR-absent dispositions (unknown floorId), not the INNER-absent ones (unknown areaId / objectId); B7 is a clean build and the naive collapse compiles; B8 is the suite and THE SUITE DOES NOT COVER THIS. The naive collapse is 'var outcome = floor.X(...); Touch(); return outcome;', which calls Touch() even when the inner operation failed. THAT IS A PERSISTED, USER-VISIBLE CHANGE, NOT A COSMETIC ONE: Touch() sets Entity.LastModified (Entity.cs:32-33), which is a mapped EF column in all four configurations (AreaConfiguration.cs:79, DungeonConfiguration.cs:48, FloorConfiguration.cs:55, PlacedObjectConfiguration.cs:40) and reaches the UI through DungeonDetailDto.LastModified and DungeonSummaryDto.LastModified via DungeonReadRepository.cs:31 and :57. NOTHING IN THE SUITE GUARDS IT, measured: grep -rn --include=*.cs "LastModified" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ returns 7 lines in 2 files -- EntityEqualityTests.cs, which asserts hash stability ACROSS a Touch, and FloorMethodsTests.cs, which asserts UpdateNumber DOES touch -- and no test asserts that a FAILED operation does not touch. So this criterion is read by a human, not caught by a test, and that is exactly why it is written down. B3 IS UNCHANGED AND STILL PERMITS ZERO: a design that removes the re-check while preserving this disposition satisfies both.
